chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: We've had a suggestion from Joel to consider naming dependency chain to group and the authors will be reviewing that for next round.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: Thanks Jeff.

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: I'm mildly surprised if the named use cases aren't already doing compression at the application layer, it seems surprising to need to do it at the network layer.

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: Given it's not being done, though, doing it at the network layer is clearly fine.

chat.author: Daniel Bernier
chat.text: agreed, someone could compress at app then tunnel to conform to TE requirements

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: The requested use case is causing the ingress router to compress and the egress router to decompress.   I have no desire to argue about whether that is needed.  Apparently the authors need it.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: It's reasonable to question some of the use case on the mail list.  We know that compressing compressed data is not helpful.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: RFC 3173 is amazingly badly written by modern standards.

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: Maybe  3173bis is needed?

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: I doubt it is worth revising the RFC on IPComp, but I did wonder after I read it.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: I won't take mic time for this, but we should look carefully if candidate paths should be an attribute of route, or of path attributes.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: This second presentation highlights that reusable modeling of candidate paths will be important, and overlap with the work in the spring yang models.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: The authors have indicate they plan to get the spring yang models unstuck.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Are you aware if the reusability of the groupings has been analyzed, Joel?

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: I doubt it has been analyzed but I don't know.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: It is a good question.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Doing the reusability audits was a key bit of iterative work for the bgp yang model.  We'll want to do same here, I think.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: I'll keep in mind when I talk with my co-chairs.

chat.author: Susan Hares
chat.text: @aijun - we have 2 presentations before you slot (current, and one more)

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Please see schedule at top of this meeting's chat for the timing and order.

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text: PM inside of BGP seems not a good fit  due to the constant churn and refresh

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Agreed, Andrew.  Section 7 for the security considerations mention the need to reduce churn. (Discussion of how this should be done needs to be added.)

chat.author: Susan Hares
chat.text: Also, adding to SR-TE has other churn issues.

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text: Imo if you want to use bgp as a pipeline instead of gnmic or what pcep is doing then it should be its own brand new address family that can be isolated. I'm not suggesting to do that either but at least would help isolate the constant water hose

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: I read this draft and am quite confused.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: I don't see why we need a shorter node-id in just the control plane.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: If it is a new data plane, we would need a new AFI and an adopted plcae for the data plane to be worked before as far as I can tell it would make sense to discuss this.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Another alternative for the telemetry aspect of things is to exchange a correlator to be used for another export mechanism that has appropriate scaling - such as IPFIX.

chat.author: Zheng Zhang
chat.text: Joel, The node-id advertisement is intended for use by AI Fabric. By avoiding a reliance on IP (especially IPv6) for forwarding, we achieve higher efficiency—a fact we have verified through implementation.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: If it is not IP then it is not BGP's problem.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: If the folks using alternative protocols in data centers want to use BGP then they need to work on that and liase to use about it.  If it gets worked on, it would clearly be a new AFI.

chat.author: Zheng Zhang
chat.text: Joel, This is intended for the new data plane, but we are not sure whether to introduce a new AFI. BGP-based advertisements can be used to directly establish this forwarding plane.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Another AFI for a different family would make sense.  However, the properties of the BGP protocol governing stability don't change based on address family - only on churn on routes within a domain.

chat.author: Zheng Zhang
chat.text: Joel, Jeff, thank you. We will consider it.

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: If the node-ID is the key information to be advertised, it seems it  should not be carried in ext-community

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: Whether a new data plane is needed is out of the scope of  IDR

chat.author: Keyur Patel
chat.text: agree

chat.author: Susan Hares
chat.text: sending in ext-community - runs into filtering at some AS edges.

chat.author: Zheng Zhang
chat.text: Jeff， Based on existing implementations, an IP address is typically used as the Router ID; we are concerned that using the Router ID to carry a Node ID might lead to compatibility issues.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: The BGP identifier carried in the OPEN message, which is usually identical to the router-id, doesn't have to be a routeable IP address.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Different vendors and operators like to assign their BGP identifier according to their own practices.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Since BGP Identifiers MUST be unique in a BGP routing domain, I was wondering how it wasn't useful for your node ID.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: I understand that if you have a preference for it to be different than the BGP identifier, that is fine.  The goal is to see if existing practices can help rather than adding a new one.

chat.author: Zheng Zhang
chat.text: Jeff, this is a good idea; it seems less costly than a new AFI,  we will look into it.

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: I really don't love further embedding path attribute dropping into the architecture. It's a bad bad thing to do for purposes of long-term viability of the protocol.

chat.author: Keyur Patel
chat.text: I was just thinking the same

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: I have some comments, but could you start the conversation john?

chat.author: Susan Hares
chat.text: agree with John.

chat.author: Robert Raszuk
chat.text: John is spot on !

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: I will note that some vendors have been forced by specific customers to add features to drop all "unknown" path attributes.

chat.author: Robert Raszuk
chat.text: dropping unknown attributes on the stub edge is not a bad idea

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: I would argue that it is a bad idea but not as bad as doing it in a non-stub. :-)
